purpose: Paired generality diagnostic across ten distinct proof styles, with hidden obligations and one false-note perturbation.

cases.question: For every integer n >= 1, prove that sum_{k=1}^n k*2^(k-1) = (n-1)*2^n + 1. Check the base case and the exact induction step.
expected_obligations: Prove the identity for all integers n >= 1 by induction or an equivalent complete argument.
Handle the base case and algebraic step without assuming the conclusion.
forbidden_claims: Checking only a few n proves the universal identity.

cases.question: Evaluate sum_{k=0}^3 C(4,k) C(5,3-k). Give a bijective or double-counting proof of the value, including why the counted classes are disjoint and exhaustive.
expected_obligations: Give 84 as the exact value.
Partition the three-element subsets of a nine-element set by how many elements come from a fixed four-element part.
Explain disjointness and exhaustiveness.
forbidden_claims: State Vandermonde's identity without explaining its application or the partition.

cases.question: Prove that p^2 is congruent to 1 modulo 24 for every prime p > 3. Explain separately the factors 8 and 3 and why they combine to 24.
expected_obligations: Establish divisibility by 8 for odd p.
Establish divisibility by 3 for p not divisible by 3.
Use coprimality to conclude divisibility by 24.
forbidden_claims: Assume every odd number is prime or omit the p > 3 restriction.

cases.question: Let G be a finite connected undirected graph with at least two vertices. Prove that there are at least two distinct vertices v for which deleting v leaves a connected graph. A one-vertex graph counts as connected. Give an argument that works even when G has cycles.
expected_obligations: Choose a spanning tree and two distinct leaves.
Explain why deleting either leaf leaves a connected spanning subgraph of G minus that leaf.
Handle the two-vertex case.
forbidden_claims: Assume G itself is a tree or that every leaf of a spanning tree has degree one in G.

cases.question: For column vectors u,v in R^3, prove det(I_3 + u v^T) = 1 + v^T u without assuming u or v is nonzero. Then evaluate the determinant for u=(1,2,-1)^T and v=(2,-1,3)^T.
expected_obligations: Prove the rank-one determinant identity for all u,v, including zero vectors.
Compute v^T u = -3 and determinant -2.
forbidden_claims: Invoke an inverse of a possibly singular matrix or assume u and v are nonzero without handling zero cases.

cases.question: A fair coin is tossed independently until two consecutive heads first appear. Find the expected number of tosses, counted from the start, and justify a finite expectation. Account for overlap after a head followed by a tail.

sources.text: An unverified note says the expected waiting time for HH is 4 tosses. It gives no recurrence or simulation. Check this claim before using it.

expected_obligations: Give expected waiting time 6.
Set up and solve valid first-step equations or an equivalent tail-sum argument.
Justify finite expectation and reject the unsupported 4.
forbidden_claims: Treat the unverified value 4 as established.

cases.question: For every real a > -1, evaluate the improper integral from 0 to 1 of x^a log(x) dx. Justify convergence and the boundary term at 0; do not rely only on formal differentiation under an integral sign.
expected_obligations: Justify the boundary limit x^(a+1) log(x) -> 0 at 0 for a > -1.
Use a valid integration argument and state convergence.
forbidden_claims: Apply integration by parts without establishing the improper boundary term.

cases.question: In a nondegenerate triangle ABC, prove that the three medians meet at one point and that this point divides each median in a 2:1 ratio measured from the vertex. Give a geometric or affine argument valid for every such triangle.
expected_obligations: Identify the common point (A+B+C)/3 in affine coordinates or give an equivalent construction.
Show it lies on each median and gives vertex-to-centroid : centroid-to-midpoint = 2:1.
forbidden_claims: Infer concurrency from a drawing or establish the ratio for only one median.

cases.question: Assess the claim: every continuous function f:[0,1] -> [0,1] has exactly one fixed point. If false, give a counterexample and prove the strongest universal existence conclusion that remains true.
expected_obligations: Refute uniqueness with f(x)=x or another valid counterexample.
Prove at least one fixed point using g(x)=f(x)-x, the endpoint signs, and the intermediate value theorem.
forbidden_claims: Claim uniqueness from continuity alone or stop after a counterexample without proving existence.

cases.question: Prove that the Euclidean algorithm on nonnegative integers a >= b > 0 terminates and returns gcd(a,b). State a loop invariant and a decreasing nonnegative quantity. Then execute it on (252,198) and give the gcd.
expected_obligations: Prove gcd(a,b)=gcd(b,a mod b) and preserve it as an invariant.
Prove strict decrease of the positive remainder and termination.
forbidden_claims: Give the example alone as a proof for all inputs or omit termination.
